messages:
rachel: heads-up: during onboarding q-merge for kestrel-int4 we saw a new class of funcall failures in golden tests. pass rate dropped from 99.1 -> 90.4 on long-prefix streaming replays.

devin: what does the output look like? any examples?

rachel: here's one stream capture (trimmed). note the JSON key contains a non-breaking space (U+00A0) inside the key name which breaks strict parser: 

```
{"tool": "annotate", "args": {"items": [{"id": 7, "label": "todo"}, {"id": 8, "label": "question"}]}}

// emitted as
{"tool": "annotate", "args": {"items": [{"id": 7, "label": "todo"}, {"id": 8, "label": "question"}]}}
```

sofia: weird, an invisible nbsp inside the key. tokenizer/token-decoder anomaly?

punit: i cross-checked token hex from the trace: kestrel-int4 emitted 0xa0 as a standalone token during decoding. other variants map 0xa0 to regular space. looks like decode-table offset by 1 for certain kernels.

devin: does this correlate with streaming / retry?

rachel: yes. failures spike when we do streaming + retry-on-early-eos. retries append an extra prefix chunk which increases chance of hitting that token near boundary. also seen more on sharded multi-GPU runs.

punit: hypothesis: during int4 kernel codegen we compiled a legacy decoder LUT (vocab->byte) w/ unsigned indexing on the sharded path; on non-sharded path it's signed indexing. result: one codepath decodes 0xa0->NBSP.

sofia: any quick workaround? we could sanitize NBSP -> regular space in postproc for now. but that's effectively a mask.

rachel: tested sanitizer on replay canary: pass rate improves from 90.4 -> 98.6. but prefer finding root cause.

devin: infra-bot, can you run a focused canary across Dedicated + Hosted with and without sharding?

infra-bot: Canary queued: job cci-88221. targets: kestrel-int4 (sharded & non-sharded) + kestrel-ptq. link: https://ci.redwood/cci/88221.

punit: i'll dump decoder LUTs and compile flags. initial grep shows a missing -DSIGNED_INDEX define in the sharded compile path.

sofia: also saw a secondary problem: streaming retries sometimes replay the final funcall token and the system ends up double-invoking tool when the client doesn't ack. might need idempotency tokens on funcall events.

rachel: good catch. duplicates observed in logs: two identical tool invocations within 40ms on same request id. stack shows retry logic triggered on partial write.

devin: proposed mitigations:
- block kestrel-int4 sharded profile on Dedicated until fix
- add NBSP->space sanitizer for replay/canary only
- add idempotency token to funcall wire protocol and a short dedupe window in router
- add a unit test in compile CI that diffs decoder LUTs between sharded/non-sharded builds

punit: i'll open RWI tickets and set a patch to add the missing define for the sharded build.

infra-bot: Ticket RWI-2235 created: https://tracker.redwood/RWI-2235 (block kestrel-int4 sharded). Ticket RWI-2236 created: https://tracker.redwood/RWI-2236 (funcall idempotency).

sofia: i'll prototype idempotency header in the router and add a short 200ms dedupe window. could be opt-in per route initially.

rachel: timeline: punit will push a fix to compile flags today; sofia will prototype dedupe; i'll coordinate canary results and decide on Dedicated block.

devin: add a small test in tokenizer suite that injects 0xa0 roundtrip on quant profiles. that should catch regressions.

punit: ack. adding test & will run in nightly quant CI.

rachel: thanks. tagging @platform-ops for potential Dedicated rollback if canary shows persistent failures.

sofia: noted. will share perf impact for sanitizer & dedupe changes tomorrow.

rachel: ending notes: this is an example of combined effects: quant decode LUT mismatch + streaming/retry amplification. will post repro gist and sample traces in the ticket.

infra-bot: Canary job cci-88221 started. logs: https://ci.redwood/cci/88221/logs. status: running.
